mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the preceding month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite sustained FEDFUNDS increases above 4% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, forward returns are negative despite the defined labor strength indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K for three consecutive months indicates improving building activity, which anticipates consumer spending and corporate investment, yielding positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during the identified housing expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month suggests supply-side shocks that reduce production capacity, causing equity risk aversion to rise and depressing 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in the month before the decision date, it indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 2% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in average hourly earnings (not available in the catalog, so this is invalid - must use existing proxies) - instead: A simultaneous decline in UNRATE and a sustained increase in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above trend suggests labor market resilience, which supports equity risk appetite and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.1% while PAYEMS increases by >2% over 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the defined labor indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available - must use existing proxies) - instead: A 3-month decline in retail sales proxies (not available) - instead: A 3-month decline in GDP deflator (not available) - instead: A 3-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with a rise in new home sales (not available) - instead: A 3-month decline in GDPC1 (demand) while FEDFUNDS remains below 4% suggests weakening demand, which lowers equity valuations and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified demand contraction phase.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the interaction between falling industrial production (INDPRO) and rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) creates a dual pressure on growth and deflation expectations, resulting in non-monotonic 60-day S&P 500 forward returns that are initially negative but can turn positive if inflation surprises persist.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising by >0.5% over 3 months AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month change > +1% for 4 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain consistently negative throughout the tightening-inflation regime.
